rule.title: ERC20 approve(spender, nonzero) without increaseAllowance or permit companion increases front-run risk

intent.attack_thesis: The contract exposes approve(address,uint256) without increaseAllowance/decreaseAllowance or EIP-2612 permit companions. When a user reduces an existing allowance, a front-running spender can spend the old allowance before the reduction, then spend the new allowance — effectively spending both.

reporting.title_template: ERC20 approve without front-run-resistant companion functions
reporting.summary: Matches ERC20 approve(address,uint256) exposure without increaseAllowance, decreaseAllowance, or EIP-2612 permit companion.
reporting.user_summary: This token uses the classic ERC20 approve() function without front-run-resistant companions. When a user tries to change a spender's allowance from X to Y, the spender can front-run the transaction to spend X before it is overwritten, then spend Y — taking X+Y total instead of Y.
reporting.technical_summary: The detector identifies contracts exposing the approve(address,uint256) selector (0x095ea7b3) without a companion increaseAllowance (0x39509351), decreaseAllowance (0xa457c2d7), or permit (0xd505accf) selector. This leaves the classic allowance race condition unmitigated.
reporting.exploit_narrative: A user approved a spender for 100 tokens and wants to reduce it to 50. The spender monitors the mempool, front-runs the reduce-approval tx with a transferFrom for 100, then lets the 50-approval land and spends that too, for 150 total instead of 50.
exploit_preconditions: user reduces allowance from nonzero to another nonzero
remediation_hints: add increaseAllowance and decreaseAllowance functions (OZ ERC20 includes these)
implement EIP-2612 permit for nonce-based, signature-protected allowance
use the approve-to-zero-first pattern in documentation and user tooling

preconditions: user has existing nonzero allowance and wants to change it

steps.action: detect user's approve(spender, Y) tx in mempool; front-run with transferFrom(user, attacker, X) spending old allowance X
steps.expected_state: old allowance X spent before reduction

steps.action: after approve(spender, Y) lands, call transferFrom(user, attacker, Y)
steps.expected_state: new allowance Y also spent; total taken = X + Y

witness_goal.success_condition: spender drains X+Y tokens when user intended to allow only Y
